Aurora to provide sample onboarding checklist and billing metadata by 2026-07-09
Security team to schedule SOC2/KMS deep-dive with Redwood security by 2026-07-14

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Redwood PM), Devon Price (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aurora PM), Luca Romano (Aurora Engineer), Helen Zhao (Aurora Security), Omar Khan (Aurora Infra)

[00:00] Jamie Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jamie from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with me i have Sanjay and Marta and Devon, hope i got all names right
[00:08] Priya Nair: thanks Jamie, priya here, we've got luke (luca) helen and omar, thanks for making time
[00:15] Jamie Chen: cool quick agenda — marketplace listing requirements, reference arch options for aurora marketplace (hosted listing vs private deploy references), security/compliance (KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs), integration points (billing metadata, onboarding), and open Qs, then next steps
[00:30] Sanjay Patel: i'll lead the technical portion, cover runtime variants and how we'd present the offering in the marketplace, quick caveat — some names in the deck are auto-gen so might say "RedWood" in places, ignore :)
[01:05] Luca Romano: ok on our side we're focused on two things: 1) quick onboarding for customers who click the marketplace listing, and 2) a reference architecture customers can click through that maps to aurora infra. we want to avoid too many manual steps.
[01:30] Marta Lopez: totally — so the marketplace listing should link to a reference architecture doc + an automated provisioning option (cloudformation/terraform module) or a contact sales flow if it's dedicated capacity
[02:10] Helen Zhao: security first question — do you support bringing-your-own-KMS, and if so what shape are the key policies? also need to confirm audit logs retention and whether we can ship logs to our SIEM (Splunk) or to our customer S3 endpoints
[03:05] Sanjay Patel: yes BYO-KMS is supported in our private deployments and in Dedicated via customer-managed KMS — typical pattern is the customer grants Redwood a KMS_encrypt/decrypt IAM role with limited scope. audit logs can stream via syslog or S3; we usually provide a connector to push to their S3 bucket or to forward events to partners like Splunk. we'll share exact perms in the security doc
[03:50] Omar Khan: any gotchas on network setup? vpc peering vs private link? we prefer interface endpoints for least friction
[04:10] Devon Price: for private flows we recommend interface endpoints (AWS privatelink) or VPC peering for hub-and-spoke setups; the ref arch will show both. important note: for low-latency we recommend co-locating customer infra and model serving region — the marketplace listing should show region compatibility
[05:00] Priya Nair: on the listing metadata — we need SKU level pricing and a usage metric to bill (per-token or per-invocation). what data do you need from us to wire billing?
[05:20] Jamie Chen: we can map to aurora SKUs. Redwood exposes usage events with resource tags and billing metadata: product_id, plan_tier, region, tokens_consumed, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens. ideally you provide a schema for the marketplace billing integration and a test endpoint we can send sample events to
[06:05] Luca Romano: we'll share the marketplace schema, but need to confirm what user identifiers you expose — we cannot pass PII in some regions, so need tokenized ids or account-level ids only
[06:35] Sanjay Patel: we can emit account_id and hashed_user_id; we avoid sending raw emails or PII in telemetry by default. we'll note that in the onboarding checklist
[07:00] Marta Lopez: switching to reference archs — we propose two customer-facing artifacts: 1) "Hosted Listing" diagram — points to Redwood hosted API with redirect to enable-sso flows; 2) "Private/Dedicated" diagram — customer-managed VPC, KMS, and optional on-prem connector. both should include network flow, auth, and data residency callouts
[07:45] Priya Nair: for hosted listing, do you have an automated provisioning flow so a customer can click "Deploy" from Aurora marketplace and get credentials + a sandbox environment?
[08:10] Sanjay Patel: yes for the hosted plan we can support an automated provisioning webhook: Aurora calls the webhook with marketplace payload, we return API key and short-lived onboarding creds. we'll need to map the payload fields — we usually need tenant_name, account_id, region, and plan_tier. for dedicated/pilot we trigger manual provisioning via ops tickets
[09:00] Luca Romano: what about the security review for marketplace — we need SOC2 attestation or similar in the listing, and a short security summary card
[09:20] Helen Zhao: also, can you confirm supported encryption at rest levels and whether logs in transit are TLS 1.2+?
[09:35] Sanjay Patel: yes TLS 1.2+ (we prefer TLS1.3 where possible). encryption at rest uses AES-256. SOC2 type 2 is available; we'll attach a redacted report for marketplace consumption and provide a longer security whitepaper for self-serve customers
[10:00] Devon Price: note — some customers ask about model artifacts and weights residency; we do not keep customer model weights unless they opt into hosting custom models. for open model variants we host model weights in our infra, but for private model hosting we can provide a BYO-model option where weights stay in the customer's bucket behind roles
[10:45] Priya Nair: that helps. on joint solutions — we were thinking a reference "LLM assistant" starter pack in the marketplace that bundles: listing + deployment templates + sample prompts + cost guide + performance benchmarks. can Redwood produce benchmark numbers for typical workloads?
[11:15] Sanjay Patel: yes we can run benchmark tests for a sample prompt set. It'll be helpful if you can provide a representative prompt corpus and expected latency SLOs (p95), throughput, and target cost per 1k tokens. we have a small harness we can run against dedicated staging infra
[12:00] Luca Romano: we'll send sample prompts; second question: we need to show quantization/instance type tradeoffs on the marketplace card — can you provide a concise table?
[12:25] Marta Lopez: yes — we'll include a simplified table: recommended instance families, typical p95 latency, throughput, and cost delta for q4 vs fp16 quantization profiles. keep it high-level for the listing, link to a deeper doc for engineers
[13:05] Helen Zhao: compliance-wise, do you support SSO via SAML and OIDC? we run SAML for internal apps
[13:20] Sanjay Patel: SAML + OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. for marketplace onboarding we can accept federated identity to provision a tenant admin and seed users via SCIM. we'll show the flow in the reference arch doc
[13:50] Priya Nair: templating — can the Terraform module accept a lot of customer-specific inputs? or do you want a minimal wrapper?
[14:10] Devon Price: we recommend a minimal module that sets up required network resources and passes a few variables to Redwood's provisioning webhook; heavy customization should be deferred to the customer's infra repo. minimal approach reduces maintenance for us and for Aurora marketplace publishers
[14:50] Jamie Chen: quick note — we need to coordinate marketing copy; Marta will take lead on the listing blurb and the features matrix, but we'll need Aurora to approve the language
[15:15] Marta Lopez: i'll draft a 2-paragraph blurb and a 5-row features matrix, share as google doc link in the follow-up. also, i'll attach a simple pricing band example so you can align with marketplace tiers
[15:45] Luca Romano: on provisioning webhooks — what's your retry behavior? some marketplace gateways will retry multiple times causing duplicates
[16:05] Sanjay Patel: we support idempotency keys; if a duplicate event arrives with the same idempotency key we return 200 and no-op. we'll document expected headers and backoff behavior in the webhook spec
[16:40] Helen Zhao: about data residency — can you pin a listing to only show regions where you can guarantee data doesn't leave the zone? we need customers in eu to be sure data stays in eu for certain SKUs
[17:05] Jamie Chen: we can tag SKUs by region and include a residency attribute. for private deployments we can specify that data never leaves customer VPC; for hosted we can offer region-restricted SKUs backed by our regional infra and note that in the listing
[17:45] Omar Khan: network egress costs for dedicated deployments — who bears them? Marketplaces often expect the application provider to define egress pricing
[18:05] Marta Lopez: typically the listing should call out that egress costs are passed through to the customer via the marketplace billing schema; Redwood provides an estimate table for common patterns but final egress billing is handled by Aurora's marketplace metering
[18:40] Priya Nair: good. next, runbook for support — can we have a joint SLA for pilot customers? sample severity levels, escalation contacts?
[19:00] Devon Price: yes we can draft a joint runbook. For pilots, we usually commit to 99.9% for hosted and lower for dedicated pilots; let's define severity 1 contacts on both sides. we'll template an escalation matrix
[19:35] Luca Romano: any known limitations for marketplace autoscale? spikes are common in our customers' use cases
[19:55] Sanjay Patel: autoscale is supported; for very spiky patterns we'd recommend burst capacity + queue smoothing. we'll include recommended autoscale policy config in the ref arch (min/max nodes, cooldowns, queue thresholds)
[20:30] Priya Nair: one more on the onboarding UI — can we present a "test credentials" button that hits a sandbox endpoint so customers can try sample prompts immediately?
[20:50] Devon Price: yes sandbox mode is standard. we generate a short-lived API key that maps to a sandbox tenant with throttled quotas; good for interactive demos
[21:15] Jamie Chen: ok let's go into the technical deep dive — Sanjay do you want to walk through the ref arch diagram on screen?
[21:30] Sanjay Patel: yep share screen — diagram: left side is aurora marketplace console -> provisioning webhook -> Redwood provisioning service. For hosted: region -> Redwood public API -> model cluster (KV cache, batching). For private: provisioning triggers VPC endpoint / privatelink -> customer VPC with interface endpoint, KMS grant to customer key, and optional on-prem connector. (audio: slight crosstalk)
[22:40] Luca Romano: can you clarify KV cache persistence? we need to know if warm cache state is recoverable across restarts for conversational workloads
[23:05] Sanjay Patel: KV cache is in-memory per model instance; we persist a checkpoint to a fast object store for warm-starts but it's not intended as long-term storage. for sticky sessions we recommend a session affinity layer or dedicated session cache. we'll include more details in doc
[23:55] Priya Nair: backup question — is session data encrypted at rest in the checkpoint store?
[24:10] Sanjay Patel: yes encryption at rest and encryption in transit; if using BYO-KMS we use customer-managed encryption keys for the checkpoint store
[24:40] Helen Zhao: audit log granularity — can we get per-request logs including request_id, api_key_id, account_id, and latency metrics? we want to feed them to our SIEM and generate alerts
[25:00] Devon Price: yes we emit request-level logs and a summarized usage stream. note we can redact prompt content per policy if needed; by default we include metadata but not raw prompt text unless customer opts in for debug mode
[25:35] Priya Nair: redaction is important for eu customers. please note that in the ref arch and onboarding checklist
[25:55] Jamie Chen: agreed. sanjay, can you call out the endpoints and sample curl for provisioning? we'll paste that in the follow-up
[26:10] Sanjay Patel: sample: curl -X POST https://provision.redwood.ai/webhook -H "Idempotency-Key: <id>" -d '{"account_id":"aurora-123","tenant_name":"ac-test","region":"eu-west-1","plan":"hosted-basic"}' -> returns api_key, tenant_id, endpoints
[26:45] Luca Romano: perfect. on metrics we want p95 latency numbers for small (256 token) and medium (2k token) prompts on recommended instance families
[27:05] Sanjay Patel: we'll run those tests; can you supply a sample corpus and target concurrency? we'll provision a staging cluster to run against
[27:30] Priya Nair: yes will share corpus + expected concurrency (start with 10 rps and then 100 rps spike profile)
[27:55] Marta Lopez: marketing/packaging question — do you have logos and legal text for marketplace? we need a publisher agreement and logo assets sized for the Aurora portal
[28:10] Jamie Chen: yes legal can provide a marketplace publisher addendum; we'll share logo assets and vendor blurb. legal might redact some of the SOC2 but we can provide a summary card for the listing
[28:45] Helen Zhao: one more thing on vulnerability disclosure — what's your cadence for pentests and do you publish a public disclosure policy?
[29:05] Sanjay Patel: we run annual pentests plus targeted tests for major releases; we have a vulnerability disclosure policy and can sign an NDA if you need. will include in security packet
[29:35] Priya Nair: ok, timeline — we want a soft launch of the listing in september 2026, is that doable?
[29:55] Jamie Chen: september is reasonable; to hit that we'll need the ref arch and onboarding artifacts by mid-July, security docs by July 14, and a joint test in August. we'll mark these milestone dates in the next steps
[30:20] Luca Romano: internal approvals on our side — marketplace review board needs the reference arch and compliance summary + a test plan. we'll send the review checklist after this call
[30:45] Devon Price: note for the joint test plan: we recommend a pilot with 3 customers, runbench for 2 weeks, and validate billing events end-to-end into Aurora staging marketplace
[31:10] Marta Lopez: feature matrix suggestion: boxes for auth (SAML/OIDC/SCIM), deployment types (hosted/dedicated/private), compliance badges (SOC2, ISO), pricing model (per-token, per-req), and support SLA. i'll draft and share
[31:45] Priya Nair: excellent — anyone have concerns about long-term maintenance of terraform modules? we don't want drift
[32:05] Sanjay Patel: recommended pattern is to version the modules and publish them in a registry; Aurora can pin a module version in the marketplace listing. we'll maintain semver and note breaking changes in release notes
[32:35] Luca Romano: how do you plan to handle marketplace upgrades for dedicated customers? we don't want service blips during upgrades
[32:55] Devon Price: for dedicated we'd do rolling upgrades, with capacity buffering and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if something regresses. We'll include rollback steps in the runbook
[33:30] Helen Zhao: data deletion policy — customers want to know how long you retain logs and how deletion requests are handled
[33:50] Sanjay Patel: default retention 90 days for logs, can be customized per contract. deletion API exists to purge customer data; for compliance requests we run a documented workflow. we'll include a short section in the security packet
[34:15] Priya Nair: good. another ops question: can we include a health check endpoint that Aurora marketplace will ping to mark the listing as healthy?
[34:35] Jamie Chen: yes we expose a /health endpoint for tenant-level health. for hosted listings we can provide a status badge; for dedicated we need a custom integration but we can push health events to marketplace status API
[34:55] Luca Romano: on the UI, can we include a "start pilot" button that opens a cal link and optionally pre-fills account info?
[35:10] Marta Lopez: yes that's straightforward. we'll add a CTA pattern: Deploy (auto-provision), Start pilot (manual), Contact sales.
[35:35] Priya Nair: are there any features you think would be hard to implement before our sept launch?
[35:50] Sanjay Patel: the BYO-model-weight hosting option is more involved (entails extra security review) so if that's in scope for sept maybe push it to a later phase. everything else — webhook provisioning, sandbox, ref arch, and metrics — are feasible
[36:15] Jamie Chen: noted — we'll scope BYO-model as phase 2. we'll push core listing and pilot tooling for phase 1
[36:40] Luca Romano: on metrics and alerts, can we surface cost-per-1000-tokens estimates on the listing and also an estimated latency range?
[36:55] Marta Lopez: yes we'll include an estimated cost band and a latency range with caveats (depends on prompt length and concurrency). we'll link to the deeper performance doc for engineers
[37:20] Priya Nair: one practical item — who will be the single point of contact for day-to-day tech questions?
[37:30] Jamie Chen: Sanjay will be primary SE contact, Marta on product, and i'll own commercial. i'll include contact list in the follow-up
[37:45] Helen Zhao: for the security deep-dive we'll want a 60-90 minute session with your security engineer; can you propose times in the week of July 13?
[38:00] Sanjay Patel: yes we'll coordinate. i'll loop in our security engineer and propose times in the next 48 hours
[38:20] Devon Price: I'll capture the ref arch variants as separate diagrams: hosted-basic, hosted-pro, dedicated-small, private-vpc. we'll attach Terraform snippets for each
[38:45] Luca Romano: regarding tests — we'll need a test harness to validate billing events in our staging — can you send a sample payload and a small python script to emit events?
[39:00] Sanjay Patel: yes sample payload and script included in repo. we'll also include guidance for idempotency keys and replay handling
[39:25] Priya Nair: ok, logistics and approvals — once we have the doc set we'll submit to marketplace review; how long do you think internal signoffs take at Redwood?
[39:40] Jamie Chen: usually 1-2 weeks for standard listings if security docs are in place; marketplace legal may add time but we try to parallelize work to meet sept
[40:05] Marta Lopez: question for Aurora — can you confirm the marketplace publisher contract timeline?
[40:15] Priya Nair: we have a 2-week window once the artifact set is complete, but internal compliance can add extra time — we will flag early if it's longer
[40:40] Luca Romano: small nit — can you include a short FAQ in the listing about limits and common gotchas? that helps with marketplace reviewers
[40:55] Jamie Chen: yes faq included — i'll draft an FAQ section covering quotas, BYO-kms caveats, privacy redaction, and upgrade notes
[41:15] Helen Zhao: two security follow-ups: 1) will you provide a redacted SOC2 and 2) can you provide encryption key rotation policy?
[41:30] Sanjay Patel: yes redacted SOC2, rotation policy is automated for our managed keys and available via KMS for BYO — we'll include sample rotation schedule and recommended roles
[42:00] Priya Nair: great. returning to joint solution packaging — can you include a sample prompts pack for an "assistant" starter kit? the playbook should have examples and cost-optimization tips
[42:20] Marta Lopez: yes we'll author a starter prompts pack and a cost-optimization one-pager (batching, prompt engineering, caching)
[42:45] Luca Romano: about caching — do you support prefix or KV-level caching and can it be exposed as a config in the Terraform module?
[43:00] Sanjay Patel: we support prefix and KV cache; we'll expose basic cache config in the module: cache_ttl, cache_size, and whether caching is enabled. advanced tuning is done in runtime config
[43:30] Priya Nair: nice. any privacy/regulatory region-specific things we should call out for the marketplace card?
[43:45] Jamie Chen: call out GDPR and data residency options; link to a compliance page. for regulated customers we recommend Private deployment and list the required attestations
[44:05] Luca Romano: can you provide an open-source example app that consumes your API we can link in the listing?
[44:15] Devon Price: yes we have a demo repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-starter) with sample terraform and example app. we'll include a small README specific to Aurora marketplace flow
[44:45] Priya Nair: that helps. OK let's go into risks — what are the top 3 technical risks you see for the sept launch?
[44:58] Sanjay Patel: 1) security docs timing (SOC2 delivery), 2) integration testing of billing events end-to-end, 3) edge case handling for idempotent provisioning across different gateway behaviors. mitigation: early security deep-dive, runbook and test harness, idempotency keys and retries in webhook spec
[45:30] Jamie Chen: agreed. we'll prioritize security and billing tests in July
[46:00] Luca Romano: any extra costs to Aurora for integration work?
[46:10] Jamie Chen: not for the basic listing work; if Aurora requests custom engineering (BYO-weight hosting, deep bespoke features) we may scope as a paid professional services engagement
[46:35] Priya Nair: good to know. quick Q: for marketplace analytics, can you expose per-listing adoption metrics to Aurora? how granular?
[46:50] Devon Price: we can share anonymized adoption metrics: installs, active tenants, avg tokens per tenant, error rates. For privacy we won't share prompt content. We can provide API or periodic CSV export
[47:15] Luca Romano: excellent. one more on rollback strategy — if a new model variant degrades quality, can we auto-fallback to a previous variant?
[47:30] Sanjay Patel: yes we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a pinned variant if regression thresholds are met. that will be part of the runbook
[47:55] Priya Nair: ok that covers most technical Qs. do you want to walk through the draft timeline?
[48:10] Marta Lopez: timeline draft: mid-July: ref arch + onboarding doc; July 14: security packet; July 20: runbook draft; Aug: integration tests and pilot; Sept: soft listing launch. we'll formalize in follow-up email
[48:40] Jamie Chen: perfect. any final blockers from Aurora?
[48:50] Helen Zhao: none immediate; we'll review docs and get back with the marketplace review checklist by EOW
[49:05] Luca Romano: we'll send corpus and schema by tomorrow
[49:20] Jamie Chen: great. recap of next steps (i'll say them and then i'll post in email): Sanjay share ref arch + webhook spec by 2026-07-07; Luca share marketplace schema and corpus by 2026-07-01; Helen share compliance items by 2026-07-10; Marta share marketing blurb + feature matrix by 2026-07-08. Security deep-dive week of 2026-07-13.
[50:05] Priya Nair: ack
[50:10] Sanjay Patel: i'll also include sample performance harness and a small python script for emitting billing events
[50:25] Jamie Chen: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a single doc bundle and calendar invites for the security deep-dive
[50:40] Devon Price: thanks all
[50:45] Priya Nair: thanks, bye
[50:50] Luca Romano: bye
[50:52] Helen Zhao: bye

[51:00] Post-call notes:
- Links mentioned: demo repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-starter (will be included in follow-up)
- Security doc link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/security/aurora-packet (to be attached)
- Reference arch doc to be shared as google drive link by Sanjay

[61:30] End of transcript
